Oil is not nearly as important as it used to be. Historically, industrialized economies ran on oil and coal, and coal existed widely, thus oil was the critical chokehold. Nowadays, advanced economies depend on many many imported things; oil is just one in a long list.

RMB is already widely used. In 2025, CIPS transaction volume was about $25T. CIPS is the clearing system for international RMB transactions, so CIPS transaction volume is the best measure of international RMB usage. Sure, CIPS doesn't see the huge international transaction volumes of some other systems, but these huge volumes are mainly caused by forex trading which is not very important. To put the $25T number in perspective, China's total trade volume in 2025 was $6.5T.

RMB is not likely to become a major reserve currency because China has capital controls. China is never going to give up capital controls because they want both a controlled exchange rate and a free hand in monetary policy. So reserve holders who want to diversify away from US control are more likely to prefer commodity reserves, especially gold reserves.
